content.text: Abscess b/n palatine tonsil & pharyngeal muscles resulting from tonsillitis or pharyngitis
CT imaging of choice to differentiate b/n abscess and cellulitis
Tonsillectomy: ⍉response to drainage, comp, recurr, or severe
▪︎deep neck space infect located behind the
midline or unilat posterior pharyngeal wall edema (MC)
▪︎anterior cervical LAD, lat neck mass or swelling
>50% of the width of adjacent vertebral body
: airway obstruct, mediastinitis, sepsis, atlantoaxial dislocation
Rapid strep or throat cx to r/o strep
: Sxtomatic (fluids, warm saline gargles, topical anesthetics, lozenges)
highest incidence of rheumatic fever if untx
pharyngeal edema or exudate, tonsillar exudate &/or petechiae
USU assoc w/ SXS of viral infect
➀ absence of cough	➂ fever >100.4°F
Infect ← EBV characterized by fever, LAD, & tonsillar pharyngitis
(known as the kissing dz) esp. ages 15-25
(may be exudative) +/- petechiae on hard palate, fatigue, HA, malaise
: airway obstruct d/t LAD, hemolytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia
TRAUMA & CONTACT SPORTS x3-4WKS TO PREVENT SPLENIC RUPTURE
